_conventions._1_read_me: English is the source language. Every key lives here first; other files are translations of this one. A key missing from a translation silently falls back to this file, so a partial translation is always safe to ship.
_conventions._2_namespaces: common.* is text reused across the admin (button labels, statuses, table chrome). admin.nav.* is the side navigation. admin.<area>.* is one page or feature area, named after its route: admin.settings.*, admin.contents.*, admin.users.*.
_conventions._3_naming: Keys describe the string's role, not its text: common.actions.save, not common.actions.save_changes. Renaming the English text should never mean renaming the key.
_conventions._4_params: Interpolation uses {{ name }}: "removed": "Removed {{ language }}". Keep parameter names meaningful — translators see them and nothing else.
_conventions._5_do_not_translate: Content-type names, user data and anything else authored in the CMS are data, not UI. Content types carry their own nameTranslations (M-D19), keyed to the site's content language, which is not this one.
_conventions._6_this_file_only: _conventions is documentation and is never rendered. Translation files do not need it.

analytics.title: Google Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Connect your GA4 property to see website analytics on the dashboard.
analytics.intro: Follow these 3 steps to connect Google Analytics to your dashboard. This is a one-time setup that takes about 5 minutes.
analytics.s1_a: Open the Google Cloud Console
analytics.s1_b: Select your Firebase project from the project dropdown at the top (it has the same name as your Firebase project)
analytics.s1_c: Go to APIs & Services → Library (or click here)
analytics.s1_d: Search for "Google Analytics API", click on it and press Enable
analytics.s1_e: Go back to the Library and also search for and enable "Google Analytics Admin API"
analytics.s2_a: In Google Cloud Console, go to APIs & Services → Credentials (or click here)
analytics.s2_b: Click + Create Credentials at the top and select OAuth client ID
analytics.s2_c: If prompted to configure the OAuth consent screen first:
analytics.s2_c1: Choose External user type and click Create
analytics.s2_c2: Fill in your App name and User support email
analytics.s2_c3: Add your email under Developer contact information
analytics.s2_c4: Click Save and Continue through the remaining steps
analytics.s2_e: Give it a name (e.g. "Arc CMS Analytics")
analytics.s2_f: Under Authorized JavaScript origins, click + Add URI and add these URLs:
analytics.s2_g: Under Authorized redirect URIs, click + Add URI and add the same URLs:
analytics.s2_i: A dialog will show your Client ID and Client Secret — copy both values
analytics.s2_j: Google will also offer to download a JSON file. You don't need the JSON file — just the Client ID and Client Secret values that you copied above
analytics.s3_a: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret in the OAuth Credentials form below and click Save Credentials
analytics.s3_b: Click the Connect Google Analytics button at the bottom of this page
analytics.s3_c: A Google popup will appear — sign in with the Google account that has access to your Analytics property and click Allow
analytics.s3_d: Your GA4 property will be detected automatically and analytics data will appear on the dashboard
analytics.why_note: Why is this step needed? Saving the credentials identifies your app to Google. The Connect button opens a Google popup where you grant permission for your app to read your Analytics data. This is a one-time authorization.
analytics.creds_hint: Enter the credentials from the Google Cloud Console. They are stored securely and only used server-side.
analytics.saved_hint: Your OAuth credentials are saved. Click below to authorize access to your Google Analytics data.
analytics.same_account: Use the same Google account that you used to create your Firebase project.
analytics.save_first: Please save your OAuth credentials above first, then you can connect to Google Analytics.
